messages:
alex: quick one — trying to switch our Node SDK to use OIDC id_tokens from the GCE metadata server for service account impersonation. calling the metadata identity endpoint with audience=https://api.redwood.run and using the returned token as Bearer, but the token-exchange step (our backend hitting oauth2/token) complains `invalid_scope`. anyone run into this? i might be mixing access vs id token flows. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/278

maria: short answer: yep, easy to mix up. id_tokens (OIDC) use `audience` not `scope`. OAuth2 access tokens use `scope`. if you call the wrong endpoint or pass `scope` when the endpoint expects `audience` you'll get errors like that. paste your minimal repro?

alex: here's the minimal client-side snippet i'm using on GCE metadata (node):
```js
const res = await fetch('http://metadata/computeMetadata/v1/instance/service-accounts/default/identity?audience=https://api.redwood.run', {
  headers: { 'Metadata-Flavor': 'Google' }
});
const idToken = await res.text();
await fetch('https://api.redwood.run/v1/ingest', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${idToken}` },
  body: JSON.stringify(payload)
});
```
response from our backend's token-exchange step: 400 `invalid_scope`.

jay: that client snippet looks correct for getting an id_token. the `invalid_scope` is probably coming from your backend where you're trying to exchange that token with the oauth2/token endpoint or calling some IAM API with a `scope` param. two common mistakes: 1) accidentally calling `metadata/instance/service-accounts/default/token?scopes=...` instead of `identity?audience=...`, or 2) feeding the id_token into a flow that expects an access_token (with scopes). The fix is to either: use the id_token directly (if the API accepts it as OIDC id_token) or do an STS token-exchange to get an access token with needed scopes.

oscar: for impersonation specifically — if you need the target SA to be impersonated (i.e., your VM's SA -> target SA), you often need to call the IAMCredentials API to `generateIdToken`/`generateAccessToken` for the target SA, or use the STS `token` exchange with `grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange` with the id_token as `subject_token`. examples: `POST https://sts.googleapis.com/v1/token` body `grant_type=...&requested_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token&subject_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt&subject_token=<id_token>&scope=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform` — this returns an access_token you can use.

maria: also note internal SDK expectations: the Redwood backend accepts either a valid OAuth2 access_token with the correct org/project claim OR an id_token where `aud` matches `https://api.redwood.run`. We also require the org scoping header for multi-tenant requests — please set `x-rw-org: <ORG_ID>` on calls that affect org-scoped resources. tokens themselves shouldn't be used to convey org/project scoping in our current model (we don't rely on org in token `claims`).

alex: ah — i wasn't setting `x-rw-org` on these test calls; thought we could put org in the token audience. thanks. one more — streaming: when i use the id_token as the Bearer for an SSE (server-sent events) stream, the stream dies after ~1m with 401s during SDK automatic retries. is that just token expiry? id_token TTL looks short (~60s on GCE).
jay: yep, id_tokens from metadata can be short. two options: 1) refresh tokens proactively in the client before expiry, or 2) for long-lived streams use an access_token with a longer TTL (via STS or impersonation) or mint a session token on the backend that is valid for the stream duration. automatic retry behavior in the SDK currently will re-try the request with the same (now-expired) token which causes repeated 401s. we added a fix on the sdk side to treat 401 from auth as a refresh-trigger and retry once after refreshing credentials (see: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/234).

oscar: follow-up practical snippets: if you're using google-auth in Python, do `id_token = google.auth.compute_engine.IDTokenCredentials(request, target_audience='https://api.redwood.run')` and that object has `.refresh(request)` helpers. for Node, use `google-auth-library`'s `getIdTokenClient(audience)` -> `client.getRequestHeaders()` to always fetch fresh tokens. avoid caching raw id_token strings for streams.

alex: good to know. i'm also worried about refresh in the middle of an active streaming connection (server-sent or websocket). recommended approach?
maria: for SSE/http streaming, you generally have to re-establish the connection after refreshing. for websocket: include a short-lived session token in the handshake and have a refresh path that opens a new ws with a new token; or rely on a server-side session token (our gateway supports issuing session tokens tied to a long-lived refresh capability). for now, pragmatic: use a longer-lived access_token for streams. we should avoid token refresh mid-stream in client lib unless we add transparent session rekeying.

ajay: (typo in name, ignore)

oscar: FYI CI/status on the PR adding auth helpers: ci-bot: build passed — https://ci.internal/redwood/sdk/278 

alex: thanks all — i'll update the PR to: add `from_service_account_impersonation()` helper (Node + Go), wire up automatic 401->refresh->retry single-retry in the requests pipeline, and add docs showing use of `x-rw-org`. will drop a follow-up for streaming token guidance. pinging @maria and @jay for review when i push. :thumbsup:
